item.title: Sounds, Alphabet, and Greetings
item.description: Lesson 1: Sounds, Alphabet, and Greetings Portuguese spelling is largely regular, but its sounds include nasal vowels and soft consonants that English speakers must practise deliberately. The alphabet has 26 letters, with k, w, and y used mainly in borrowed words. The five vowels — a, e, i, o, u —…

item.title: Ser, Estar, Ter, and Describing Yourself
item.description: Lesson 2: Ser, Estar, Ter, and Describing Yourself Portuguese has two verbs for "to be," and choosing between them is a core skill. Ser is used for identity, origin, profession, inherent characteristics, time, and material: Eu sou professora (I am a teacher), Ele é brasileiro (He is Brazilian), São…

item.title: Regular Verbs in the Present Tense
item.description: Lesson 3: Regular Verbs in the Present Tense Portuguese verbs fall into three conjugations: -ar (falar, to speak), -er (comer, to eat), and -ir (partir, to leave). The present tense covers both "I speak" and "I am speaking" in most everyday use, though estar + gerund (estou falando) marks an action…

item.title: Articles, Nouns, and Gender
item.description: Lesson 4: Articles, Nouns, and Gender Every Portuguese noun has a gender — masculine or feminine — and the article must match it. Learn every new noun with its article: o livro (the book), a caneta (the pen), o estudante, a amiga. Definite articles (the): masculine singular o, feminine singular a…

item.title: The Past Tense — Pretérito Perfeito
item.description: Lesson 5: The Past Tense — Pretérito Perfeito Portuguese tells completed past actions mainly with the pretérito perfeito, formed with a single word whose endings change by conjugation. For regular -ar verbs, falar gives: eu falei, você/ele/ela falou, nós falamos, vocês/eles/elas falaram. Note that…

item.title: Food, Ordering, and Quantities
item.description: Lesson 6: Food, Ordering, and Quantities Food vocabulary is practical and culturally rich. Key words: o pão (bread), o queijo (cheese), a manteiga (butter), a carne (meat), o peixe (fish), a fruta (fruit), os legumes (vegetables; Brazil also uses verduras), o arroz (rice), o feijão (beans), a…

item.title: Future, Plans, and the Weather
item.description: Lesson 7: Future, Plans, and the Weather Portuguese expresses the future in two main ways, and the informal one dominates speech. The most common spoken future uses ir (to go) in the present plus the infinitive: Vou estudar português (I am going to study Portuguese / I will study Portuguese), Vamos…

item.title: Travel, Directions, and Everyday Conversation
item.description: Lesson 8: Travel, Directions, and Everyday Conversation Travel Portuguese brings together everything so far: polite requests, numbers, directions, and past and future tenses. Transport words: o trem (train, Brazil) / o comboio (train, Portugal), o ônibus (bus, Brazil) / o autocarro (bus, Portugal)…
